McLaren: McLaren has tweaked the front suspension to smooth the airflow over the car, giving the front end a tighter, more responsive feel through the corners. The front‑corner geometry has also been refined, sharpening turn‑in and helping the tyres stay in their optimal grip window. At the rear, the team has re‑balanced the mechanical setup, improving stability under braking and on the exit, which should translate into more consistent lap times around this weekend’s circuit.
Scuderia Ferrari: Ferrari has tweaked the underside of the car – the floor fences now have a different shape and tilt, the “boat‑like” floor has been reshaped with a wider tunnel, the front edge wing is shorter and angled differently, and the diffuser at the rear has been re‑designed for a larger volume. All of these changes tighten up the airflow under the car, giving more down‑force and less drag, so the drivers should have better grip and higher cornering speeds right out of the gates this weekend.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has added a fresh patch on the floor edge with a small vent just in front of each rear tyre, smoothing the airflow under the car and boosting down‑force where it counts most. This tweak should give the RB a tighter rear‑end and better grip through the high‑speed corners, helping the drivers extract a few extra tenths on the weekend’s lap times. In short, it’s a subtle aero upgrade aimed at keeping the car stable and quicker on the track.
Mercedes F1 Team: Mercedes has fitted a bigger brake‑duct opening at the front corners and a larger exit slot on the rear bodywork – both tailored for this circuit’s cooling demands. The extra airflow will keep the brakes and power unit from overheating, letting the drivers push harder for longer. In short, it’s a temperature‑management tweak that should translate into more consistent lap times this weekend.
